title: Booking an Airport Ride for Someone Else: A Passenger Handoff Checklist
description: Booking an airport ride for a guest, colleague or family member? Use this checklist and passenger message to keep flight details, pickup and contacts clear.
cta: Arrange a clear pickup for your passenger.
image_alt: Paper-style illustration of a checklist, a phone with a location pin, a rolling suitcase and an airplane connected by an orange line.
body:
When you book an airport ride for someone else, make sure the operator knows who is traveling and the passenger knows how to find the ride. A confirmation in your inbox is not enough if the traveler lands without the pickup instructions or a working contact number.

Whether you are arranging a colleague's arrival in San Jose, a guest's pickup at Oakland or a family member's ride from SFO, use one short trip brief. Send it to the passenger before departure and keep the operator's version consistent with it.

Separate the booker from the passenger

Give the operator the actual passenger's name and mobile number, including the country code, with their permission. Identify yourself as the booker and provide a backup contact who will be reachable during the arrival window. If you will be in a meeting or asleep in another time zone, choose someone else for that role.

Ask where the confirmation and pickup updates will go. Do not assume that entering your email address also sends instructions to the traveler. Keep billing and receipt arrangements clear separately; the passenger should not need to resolve an administrative question while looking for the car.

Build one accurate trip brief

  • Arrival airport and date: use the airport code, such as SJC, OAK or SFO, and the local arrival date. For an overnight flight, check that you have not copied the departure date.
  • Flight: include the airline and flight number for the final flight into the pickup airport. If the itinerary shows a codeshare, include the operating airline and flight number when available.
  • Timing: record the scheduled landing time and the pickup arrangement agreed with the operator. Label each clearly; they are not necessarily the same time.
  • Passenger and luggage: give the number of travelers, suitcases and bulky items. Disclose a stroller, child-seat request or assistance requirement before booking and confirm what can be accommodated.
  • Destination: use the full street address and the correct hotel or building entrance. Include any necessary access instructions.
  • Contacts: list the passenger, the operator's day-of-trip contact and the reachable backup booker.
  • Confirmation: keep the reservation reference, agreed pickup instructions and applicable change and waiting terms together.

For example, an organizer booking a visitor into SJC for a Palo Alto meeting should send the final inbound flight details, the visitor's mobile number and the office entrance. Sending only the meeting time and office name leaves the arrival coordination unresolved. This is a planning example, not a promise about journey time.

Give the passenger the pickup instructions for the booked service

A sign for taxis or app-based rides does not necessarily identify the pickup point for a prearranged chauffeur. For example, SJC's official limousine guidance distinguishes reserved limousine locations from the app-based pickup locations used by Uber Black and Lyft Black. Do not send the passenger toward a familiar rideshare area without checking the reservation instructions.

Use our San Jose airport pickup page or Oakland airport pickup page for planning context, then confirm the terminal and pickup point with the operator. If the instructions and current airport signage appear inconsistent, contact the operator before moving to a different location.

Send a message the passenger can save

Replace the bracketed fields below with confirmed details. Send the message before the traveler boards, and ask them to acknowledge receipt. A saved screenshot or offline note helps when a data connection is unavailable.

Your airport ride
Arrival: [airport code], [local arrival date], [airline and flight number].
Ride confirmation: [operator and reservation reference].
Destination: [full address and entrance].
Pickup plan: [confirmed instructions, or how and when updated instructions will be supplied].
After landing: let [agreed contact] know when you have your bags and are ready to follow the pickup instructions.
Need help: [operator's day-of-trip phone number]. Backup: [booker's name and number].
If your flight or arrival airport changes, tell [designated coordinator] as soon as you know.

Ask the operator how the passenger should verify the assigned chauffeur and vehicle before getting in. Do not include payment-card details or unnecessary personal documents in the trip brief.

Decide who handles changes

Choose one person to coordinate changes with the operator. Flight tracking can help with a delayed arrival, but it does not replace telling the operator that the traveler has rebooked onto a different flight, changed airports or changed the destination.

If you make a change as the booker, obtain the operator's confirmation and send the updated plan to the passenger. Avoid leaving the driver, traveler and coordinator with three different versions of the itinerary. Review any revised price or terms before treating the change as accepted.

Plan for the gap between landing and being ready

The traveler may still need to leave the aircraft, collect bags or complete arrival formalities. Agree on how they will report that they are ready, and tell the operator if baggage or another issue is taking longer than expected. Check the reservation's waiting terms rather than assuming every delay is included.

If the passenger's phone will not work on arrival, arrange a communication fallback before departure. That might mean a reachable traveling companion or an agreed way to contact the operator using airport Wi-Fi. Confirm the arrangement with both parties; do not make an improvised terminal meeting point the fallback.

Make the last check a two-way check

Before travel, confirm that the operator has the passenger details and that the passenger has the ride details. That short exchange closes the gap between a booking being made and a traveler being ready to use it.

To arrange a ride, review Koast airport transfers and send the flight, passenger, luggage and destination details to reserve@koastride.com. Make clear that you are booking for another person and ask for the pickup instructions to share.
